question.text: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)
question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the last available daily value of the U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity published on the [FRED website](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) for the final calendar day (typically the final Friday) of the corresponding biweekly period.
question.fine_print:
* If the FRED data is delayed, the value will be taken as soon as published for the relevant date.
* If the market is closed on the scheduled ending date or if no value for that date is published by FRED for two weeks, the most recent available value from an earlier day in the period will be used.
* Only the initially published value for each date will be used (no revisions).
* The value is reported in percentage points.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-07: FRED DGS10 shows the latest value as **4.84% for 2026-11-05**. The value for Nov 6 was not yet posted. The five most recent values: 10-30 4.94, 11-02 4.91, 11-03 4.95, 11-04 4.90, 11-05 4.84. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10)
- The question resolves on the **initially published** FRED value for Friday 2026-11-20.
- Recent path, re-aligned by me from FRED's text file (its export put each value one row off; the main FRED page confirms the corrected alignment): peak 5.31 on about Oct 2, 5.28 on about Oct 6, 5.21 on Oct 9, 5.09 on Oct 16, 5.00 on Oct 23, 4.94 on Oct 30. That is a drop of about 47 bp from the peak. [FRED txt](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/DGS10.txt)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The value will be set by the close on Nov 20, 10 trading days from now. The bond market is likely closed Wed Nov 11 for Veterans Day (my assumption, not verified).
- 2026-11-06 (intraday or close, not yet on FRED): the 10Y rose about 3 to 4 bp to roughly **4.87% (reports range from 4.855% to 4.878%)** after the jobs report. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/us-treasuries-stumble-as-strong-labor-market-lifts-fed-hike-bets), [newsbytes](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/us-10-year-yield-hits-4855-after-october-jobs-report/tldr), [pomegra](https://pomegra.io/news/10-year-treasury-yield-hits-487-after-strong-jobs-data)
- Caveat: a 24/7 Wall St item says "4.90%" on Nov 6. It is probably stale, so treat it with caution.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-06: The October jobs report showed payrolls up 165k against about 59k to 65k expected. Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. The 2Y was about 4.52-4.54% and the 30Y about 5.27-5.28%. Futures priced roughly 75% odds of a December Fed hike. [Finimize](https://finimize.com/content/strong-us-jobs-report-pushed-treasury-yields-higher), [beinsure](https://beinsure.com/news/us-jobs-report-165k-payroll-lift-treasury-yields/)
- 2026-11-06: Safe-haven buying around the world. The Bund hit 3.208%, its lowest since late August, and China's 10Y hit a record low of about 1.6%. [n-tv](https://www.n-tv.de/wirtschaft/der_boersen_tag/Renditen-globaler-Anleihen-sinken-bei-Flucht-in-Sicherheit-id31502917.html)
- 2026-11-05: The 10Y fell 5.7 bp to 4.837%, its lowest close in almost two months. This came during a tech and AI sell-off after Democrats won both houses in the midterms (reports say Nasdaq 100 -5.9%, S&P -3.8%). [finanznachrichten](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-11/70051040-ten-year-treasury-yield-slumps-to-lowest-level-in-almost-two-months-020.htm), [talkmarkets](https://talkmarkets.com/article/gold-rallies-above-4100-as-nasdaq-100-crashes-december-hike-bets-fade)
- Conflicting reports: a Seeking Alpha item says stocks *rallied* on Nov 5 after the Democratic sweep. This contradicts the other sources, which describe a sell-off. I could not resolve the conflict.
- October 2026: The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with two dissents in favor of a hike. September CPI (released Oct 14) came in hot. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/14/cpi-inflation-report-september-2026.html), [Axis](https://axis-intelligence.com/fed-rate-hike-odds-statistics/)

## 4. Base rates
- Statistical baseline: 10-trading-day changes since 2005, with the last 3 years weighted double, give a distribution for Nov 20 centered on 4.84. p5 4.58, p10 4.64, p25 4.74, p50 4.84, p75 4.95, p90 5.05, p95 5.11. That is roughly ±10 bp for the middle half and ±25 bp for the 5-95 range. If Nov 6 closed near 4.87%, shift the center up by about 3 bp.
- Recent volatility is high: -17 bp on Oct 23, +15 bp from Sep 24 to 25, and -6 bp on Nov 5.
- Trend: yields have fallen steadily since early October (5.31 to 4.84).
- Seasonality: 10Y yields have no meaningful seasonal pattern, so I did not compile earlier years' early-to-late November moves.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, 10Y on Mon Nov 9 (prices from Nov 7): about 51% for ≥4.87, 46% for ≥4.89, 62% for ≥4.83, 84% for ≥4.77, 19% for ≥4.95. The implied median is about 4.87.
- Kalshi, November low: about 50% for ≤4.75-4.76. November high: about 30% for ≥5.06, 21% for ≥5.10.
- Polymarket, November low: 76% below 4.82, 54% below 4.76, 34% below 4.70. November high: 35% for 5.06, 21% for 5.17, 9.5% for 5.25. The 5.13 rung at 42% looks inconsistent with its neighbors, probably because it is illiquid.
- Kalshi, Dec 31 2027: about 51% for ≥5.00.
- Manifold has a market on the Nov 30 FRED value ([link](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/where-will-the-10year-treasury-yiel)). I did not retrieve its prices.
- I found no market that resolves directly on the Nov 20 value, and no sell-side point forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before Nov 20
- Mon 2026-11-09: 3-year note auction. [Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0678)
- Tue 2026-11-10: **October CPI**, 8:30 ET per secondary sources (I did not confirm on the BLS site). The **$42B 10-year auction** is the same day at 1:00 ET. [financefeeds](https://financefeeds.com/gold-price-today-4045-saturday-week-ahead-after-165000-jobs-december-hike-odds-cpi-10-november-bull-4135-bear-3990/), [Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0678)
- Wed 2026-11-11: Veterans Day, likely a bond market holiday.
- Thu 2026-11-12: 30-year bond auction. Refunding auctions settle Nov 16. [Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0678)
- Mid-November: PPI, retail sales and Fed speakers are likely, but I did not confirm the dates. The October FOMC minutes would usually come out about three weeks after the meeting, so possibly around Nov 18. The next FOMC is Dec 9 (some sources say Dec 8-9).
- Ongoing: the post-midterm equity and AI sell-off and safe-haven flows, against strong labor data and roughly 75-80% odds of a December hike.

## Research brief: 10-year Treasury yield, period ending Fri Nov 20, 2026

The yield sits at 4.86% as of Nov 6, about in the middle of the question's range. The question will be decided by the DGS10 value FRED publishes for Nov 20.

### 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on FRED's DGS10 value for 2026-11-20. Nov 20 is a Friday and a normal trading day. FRED takes this series from the Treasury par yield curve. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/DGS10.txt)
- 2026-11-05: the latest value on FRED is **4.84**. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/DGS10.txt)
- 2026-11-06: Treasury.gov's 10-year par yield is **4.86** (2-year: 4.51). FRED should show this same value for Nov 6 once it updates. [Treasury.gov](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value_month=202611)
- Recent FRED values:
  - Sep 22: 4.96
  - Sep 30: 5.29
  - Oct 5: **5.31**, the autumn peak
  - Oct 13: 5.21
  - Oct 21: 5.13
  - Oct 22: 4.96
  - Oct 28: 5.05
  - Oct 30: 4.94
  - Nov 2: 4.91
  - Nov 3: 4.95
  - Nov 4: 4.90
  - Nov 5: 4.84

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Ten trading days remain, and the yield sits in the lower-middle of the 4.255 to 6.255 range.
- One collected article says the yield "fell to 4.90% on Nov 6." That doesn't match the official data (4.86) and looks unreliable.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-06: October payrolls rose by 165,000, against roughly 59,000 to 65,000 expected. Unemployment fell to 4.1%. The 10-year rose about 3 to 4 bp intraday to around 4.87%, and the 2-year rose up to 7 bp to 4.54%. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/us-treasuries-stumble-as-strong-labor-market-lifts-fed-hike-bets), [Le Private Banker](https://leprivatebanker.com/2026/11/06/treasuries-slip-as-payrolls-beat-lifts-fed-december-hike-bets-near-70-unwinding-part-of-thursdays-haven-rally/)
- 2026-11-06: futures put the chance of a 25 bp Fed **hike** in December at about 70 to 80%. Markets priced at least 40 bp more tightening by Sep 2027. A headline says Fed official Daly expects more tightening is likely. [Le Private Banker](https://leprivatebanker.com/2026/11/06/treasuries-slip-as-payrolls-beat-lifts-fed-december-hike-bets-near-70-unwinding-part-of-thursdays-haven-rally/), [Finimize](https://finimize.com/content/strong-us-jobs-report-pushed-treasury-yields-higher)
- 2026-11-05: buyers fled to safe assets after Democrats swept Congress in the midterms and worries grew about AI spending. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 5.9% (the S&P 500 fell 3 to 3.8%). The 10-year fell about 6 bp to 4.84%, its lowest close in almost two months. [TalkMarkets](https://talkmarkets.com/article/gold-rallies-above-4100-as-nasdaq-100-crashes-december-hike-bets-fade), [finanznachrichten](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-11/70051040-ten-year-treasury-yield-slumps-to-lowest-level-in-almost-two-months-020.htm)
- 2026-10: the Fed held rates at 3.75 to 4.00% in October, with two officials voting to hike. The 10-year fell about 36 bp over October. [FinanceFeeds](https://financefeeds.com/gold-price-today-4045-saturday-week-ahead-after-165000-jobs-december-hike-odds-cpi-10-november-bull-4135-bear-3990/), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield/news/596893)

### 4. Base rates
- The code-computed baseline below uses 10-day changes in FRED data since 2005, with the last 3 years weighted double. It is centred on the Nov 5 value of 4.84:

| p90 | 5.05 |
| p95 | 5.11 |

  Re-centred on 4.86, the p50 would be about 4.86. The typical 10-day standard deviation is about 15 to 16 bp.
- The market has been more volatile than usual lately:
  - Sep 22 to Oct 5: up 35 bp
  - Oct 21 to Oct 22: down 17 bp in one day
  - Oct 5 to Nov 5: down 47 bp
- The trend since early October is down, but the strong jobs report and the priced-in hike pulled it back up partly.
- Seasonality: the 10-year yield has no real seasonal pattern, so I did not compile year-by-year changes from early to late November.

### 5. Other forecasts
These are Kalshi and Polymarket prices collected on 2026-11-07.
- **Kalshi, Nov 9 close:** P(≥4.87%) is 0.51, so the median is about 4.87. P(≥4.77) is 0.84 and P(≥4.95) is 0.19. This is a one-day market, not the Nov 20 close.

- **Polymarket, November low:** P(below 4.82) is 0.76, P(below 4.76) is 0.54 and P(below 4.70) is 0.34. These look somewhat stale, because 4.84 has already traded.
- **Manifold, Nov 30 close:** a market exists ([link](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/where-will-the-10year-treasury-yiel)), but I did not get its prices.
- **Kalshi, Dec 31, 2027:** median about 5.0%.
- I found no sell-side forecast specific to Nov 20.

### 6. Upcoming events before Nov 20
- 2026-11-10 (Tue): October CPI, the last CPI report before the Dec 8 to 9 FOMC meeting. One forecast expects headline +0.28% and core +0.21% month on month, and says a softer core print would still leave its December hike call intact. [FinanceFeeds](https://financefeeds.com/gold-price-today-4045-saturday-week-ahead-after-165000-jobs-december-hike-odds-cpi-10-november-bull-4135-bear-3990/)
- 2026-11-11 (Wed): Veterans Day. The bond market is normally closed, but I did not confirm this for 2026.
- Unconfirmed: the quarterly refunding auctions (3-, 10- and 30-year) usually fall in the second week of November. I did not find the 2026 dates.
- Likely mid-November: PPI, retail sales and the October FOMC minutes (usually about 3 weeks after the meeting, so around Nov 18). I did not find confirmed dates.
- Ongoing risks:
  - More AI-related stock selloffs or safe-haven buying (as on Nov 5)
  - Fed officials talking up hikes (Daly)
  - Fiscal or policy news after the midterms
  - Oil prices

I could not get the Nov 6 closing level from a market wrap, so the 4.86 figure comes from Treasury.gov only.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 2 weeks. The resolving value is the initially published FRED close for Friday, Nov 20, 2026. That is 9 trading days after Nov 6, assuming the bond market is closed for Veterans Day on Nov 11.

(b) The latest value on FRED is 4.84% for Nov 5, 2026. Reports put the Nov 6 close at about 4.86-4.88% after the strong jobs report; that value is not yet on FRED.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be about 4.87.

(d) Yields have fallen from 5.31 in early October to 4.84, roughly 3-4 bp per trading day on average lately. Extrapolating that trend gives about 4.60-4.65. However, the jobs report and roughly 75% odds of a December hike push against continuing the decline.

(e) Historically, 10-trading-day changes give a middle-half range of about ±10 bp and a 5-95 range of about ±25 bp. Recent volatility has been above average, for example -17 bp in one day on Oct 23. October CPI and the 10-year auction both fall on Nov 10, and there is ongoing post-midterm equity turbulence.

(f) Market signals:
- Kalshi's market for Monday Nov 9 implies a median of about 4.87.
- Markets on the November low imply about a 50% chance of trading at or below about 4.75.
- Markets on the November high imply about a 30% chance of reaching at or above 5.06.
- Taken together, these suggest a fairly symmetric, wide distribution centered in the mid-to-high 4.8s.
